observed_vs_expected: The pre-execution hypothesis predicted a monotonic rise in best_target_score as thickness optimization decoupled the two spectral bands. The latest measurement represents a lower-direction deviation, falling 0.1809 points below the historical peak achieved in round 4. Contrary to expectations of steady convergence or a clean failure, valid_candidates remained stable at 9 and tightest_margin held at 0.4137, indicating the design space remains physically feasible rather than collapsing.
deviation_mechanism: The score volatility is caused by unbounded optical thickness perturbations that shift the stack's phase accumulation across multiple Fabry-Pérot resonance orders. When specific layer thicknesses jump by >15–50 nm between iterations, the effective n·d product rapidly crosses quarter/half-wave conditions. This forces the aperiodic interference pattern to flip abruptly between constructive and destructive states in the 800–1500 nm window, destroying the gradual band-decoupling the optimizer seeks and manifesting as the observed wild score swings rather than asymptotic convergence.
continue_rationale: Six executable rounds have been completed, yet the optimization trajectory shows no plateau or exhaustion; scores swing by nearly 0.18 points per cycle. With tightest_margin comfortably above the 0.05 threshold (0.4137) and valid_candidates stable at 9, there is ample feasible surface area to explore. Continuing with a modified search regime that actively suppresses the identified thickness instabilities can convert this chaotic oscillation into targeted refinement toward the established 0.75 peak.
insight_for_next: Lock the search bounds for the four most volatile layer indices (10, 14, 16, 18) to ±15 nm around their median historical values to prevent resonance-flipping phase jumps. Keep all other layers unconstrained to maintain degree-of-freedom diversity, and re-enable the standard optimizer to allow fine-grained adjustment within the newly dampened subspace.

Bounding these specific indices eliminates the root cause of the interference regime switching while preserving the route's capacity for incremental spectral shaping.
